grh_ab44f09eb4cfe6714c8e.title: Leave It To Love
paragraphs: Randy Foster returns to Rivers End after losing both feet in combat. Army rehabilitation has taught him to use artificial feet confidently, he is preparing to return to work, and he wants an ordinary life rather than constant reminders that he is different. His wife Ellen, however, cannot stop protecting him, worrying over steps, drafts, traffic and every small exertion until her sympathy becomes suffocating. Randy asks Dr. Christian to help her see that he is capable, while Ellen separately complains that Randy refuses the special care she thinks he needs. Christian mischievously turns the situation around so that each begins treating the other as the fragile one. Randy fusses over Ellen, insists she rest and takes over the household, while Ellen experiences firsthand how oppressive excessive solicitude can feel. The scheme collapses when Christian and Judy arrive and learn the real reason Ellen has not been feeling well: she is pregnant. With a baby genuinely on the way, the couple's roles and worries find a more natural balance, and Christian admits that love and nature have solved the problem better than his meddling could.

grh_ab0e588e83f448f9d2cf.title: The Singular Affair of the Baconian Cipher
paragraphs: A strangely typeset notice in the Times uses Francis Bacon's bilateral cipher to spell out a plea for help from the wealthy, paralyzed Mr. Quilter. Holmes, Watson and French detective Francois La Vier visit the estate, where a man claiming to be Quilter dismisses the message as bait for a Shakespeare authorship researcher. Fresh earth on the supposed invalid's boots proves he is an impostor. The conspirator is Quilter's relative David, who stands to inherit and has been terrorizing the old man with an accomplice. After impersonating Quilter, David drugs the real victim and hides him in his own wheelchair, assuming it is the last place anyone will look. Watson notices the breathing man, saving Quilter before the pair can murder him.

grh_ab9d3068bac041930a72.title: The Storm
paragraphs: Discouraged after losing a patient he could not move to a properly equipped hospital, Dr. Christian broods over the money Rivers End lacks for specialists and better rural medical care. He falls asleep as a storm gathers and dreams that Dan Foster and his sister Blanche offer him a fortune to alter Blanche's face so she can impersonate a missing heiress and steal a million-dollar inheritance. The promised fee could finance nearly everything Christian has been wishing he could provide for his patients, making the temptation more dangerous than simple greed. He refuses the fraud, and Dan finally pulls a gun and threatens both Christian and Blanche unless the operation is performed. Christian still refuses. A crash of thunder wakes him before the gun can fire, and the dream leaves him reassured that limited resources do not excuse wrongdoing and that doing whatever good he can with what he has is still worthwhile.

grh_ab9669e3e05f27ee9da0.title: Quiet City
paragraphs: When Britt returns to Quiet City, he finds a once-violent frontier town growing into a settled community but its old sheriff still expects the people to behave as they did years before. After Pike kills rancher Jason Norton in a cattle dispute, Britt helps the sheriff capture him alive, while the sheriff worries that Jason's brother and an angry crowd will lynch the prisoner. Instead the townspeople insist that Pike receive a fair trial and let the courts punish him. Britt points out that Quiet City has grown up largely because its sheriff spent years teaching people to respect the law.

paragraphs: A boatman named Peter is hired to help recover a missing briefcase in a coastal jungle region torn by armed revolution. His clients insist the case contains sensitive political papers, but after capture, escape and a dangerous return to the hiding place, Peter becomes convinced they are lying.
